- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., 0.00 or negative) and model still forecasts high prices, adjust downward by 5–10% to reflect bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 85% of prior peak or 10% below recent high.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75% of recent average), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of downward correction.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to align with volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of 30-day average, model overestimates; apply 5–10% downward bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 0.00 or 0.33) followed by recovery, model often misses the dip; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in correction.
